description: The PICTURE character-string length bound (ISO §2023:13.18.40.3 SR4: 63 characters in the 2023 text) is 30 below COBOL-2002 - a RELAXATION, so a 31-to-50-character character-string-1 compiles at 2002 and later and is rejected at COBOL-85 with COBOL2146 (also under --permissive: a length error, not a removed construct), the word-length row's posture. THE EDGE IS QUOTED for the 2002 half and DERIVED for the 85 half (VCR row 7.46; the repo holds no 1985 text, ratified decision #1): the 2002 draft's own 13.16.38.2 SR4 reads 'The maximum number of characters allowed in character-string-1 is 50' and its Annex F.2 item 94 records 'The maximum number of characters that may be specified in a picture character-string is increased from 30 to 50'; GnuCOBOL 3.2's cobol85.conf carries pic-length 30 (kb/Work R61's method). ONE bound, PictureAnalyzer.MaxStringLength(edition), read by Analyze's prologue (kb/Work PB4304).
display: a PICTURE character-string longer than 30 characters
citation: ISO §2023:13.18.40.3 SR4 (the character-string length bound; 63 in the 2023 text) - the 30-character bound at COBOL-85 is DERIVED (VCR row 7.46)
vcr: VCR row 7.46 (PICTURE character-string bound 30 -> 50 at 2002); kb/Work PB4304
